mainTopic: Does 'he could have sprinkled' count as sprinkling, for פיגול and טומאת אוכלין according to רבי שמעון, and why do מעילה and טומאה differ?
overview: The גמרא tests whether רבי שמעון's idea that 'if he wanted, he could redeem it' also works for sprinkling blood. If it did, a sacrifice made פיגול during the זריקה would count as having been fit to eat beforehand, so it should be susceptible to טומאת אוכלין. Yet the ברייתא says פיגול is not susceptible. The first answer limits the ברייתא to פיגול during שחיטה. It then explains that the ברייתא needed the מנחה case to teach that a מנחה is susceptible even when made פיגול at the קמיצה, because the flour was fit to eat before it became holy. רב אשי gives a different answer: רבי שמעון uses 'if he wanted' only for redeeming, never for sprinkling. The גמרא challenges him from רבי יהושע's rule about מעילה, whose wording suggests that blood which could have been sprinkled counts as a time of being permitted. רב אשי answers that מעילה and טומאה work differently. Holiness that has left never returns, but food status depends on whether the blood can still be sprinkled. The גמרא then begins a new challenge from a משנה about an אשם תלוי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If the blood could have been sprinkled, why is the meat not susceptible?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge: under רבי שמעון's rule, blood ready to be sprinkled counts as sprinkled, so why does the ברייתא say פיגול meat is not susceptible to טומאת אוכלין? Isn't the case one of פיגול during זריקה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had wanted, he could have sprinkled the blood. Yet the ברייתא teaches that the meat is not susceptible to the impurity of food. Isn't the ברייתא talking about a case where he made it פיגול during the sprinkling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing a challenge. If רבי שמעון's 'if he wanted' idea also applies to sprinkling, so that blood ready to be sprinkled counts as sprinkled, the ברייתא's ruling seems to clash with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only receive טומאת אוכלין if it had a moment when it was fit to eat. If the פיגול thought came only at the זריקה, then before that moment the blood was ready to be sprinkled and so counts as sprinkled. That means the meat was already fit, so it should be susceptible. Yet the ברייתא says it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood of a sacrifice on the מזבח
The impurity that food can receive
A sacrifice disqualified by a wrong intention to eat or offer it after its proper time
Isn't it that…? (a way of pushing a reading of a source)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a challenge that began just before it. 'If he wanted, he could sprinkle' is the גמרא's suggestion that רבי שמעון's 'if he wanted, he could redeem' idea extends to sprinkling. רב אשי later rejects that extension (step 6).

phrases.english: and if he had wanted, he could have sprinkled,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is testing whether רבי שמעון's 'if he wanted, he could redeem' idea also works for sprinkling, so that blood ready to be sprinkled counts as sprinkled.

phrases.english: and yet it teaches that it is not susceptible to the impurity of food.
What, is it not where he made it פיגול during the sprinkling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge that began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that פיגול meat is not susceptible to טומאת אוכלין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under כל העומד לזרוק כזרוק דמי, פיגול during זריקה means the meat counted as fit beforehand, so it should be susceptible.

steps.title: The ברייתא is talking about פיגול during slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a case where the פיגול thought happened during the שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The ברייתא is talking about a case where he made it פיגול during the slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the ברייתא to פיגול during שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the meat became פיגול already at the שחיטה, the blood never stood ready to be sprinkled in a fit way. So the meat never had a moment of being fit, and רבי שמעון's rule does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering the animal, the first main service of a sacrifice

phrases.english: No, it is where he made it פיגול during the slaughtering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא might have been about פיגול during זריקה, which would clash with רבי שמעון's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about פיגול during שחיטה, where the meat was never fit.

steps.title: So what if it was made פיגול during sprinkling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law would be for פיגול during זריקה, and suggests that it would indeed be susceptible to טומאת אוכלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he made it פיגול during the sprinkling, what is the law? Is it indeed susceptible to the impurity of food?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws out what the answer in step 2 implies. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא is limited to פיגול during שחיטה, it follows that פיגול during זריקה should be susceptible to טומאת אוכלין. The גמרא states this result so it can test it against the wording of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: So too / indeed so

phrases.english: But if he made it פיגול during the sprinkling, what is the law?
Is it indeed susceptible to the impurity of food?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what the answer in step 2 implies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The law for פיגול during זריקה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It would seem to be susceptible to טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: Then the ברייתא should have made the distinction within the animal case
steps.stepSummary: If פיגול during זריקה is susceptible, the ברייתא should have drawn that contrast inside the animal case instead of switching to a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Instead of teaching that if he made a מנחה פיגול it is susceptible to the impurity of food, let the ברייתא draw the distinction within the animal case itself: When is this said? When he made it פיגול during the slaughtering. But if he made it פיגול during the sprinkling, it is susceptible to the impurity of food!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea from step 3 by looking at how the ברייתא is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא contrasts animal פיגול, which is not susceptible, with a מנחה, which is. If there were also a susceptible case among animal sacrifices themselves (פיגול during זריקה), the ברייתא should have mentioned that closer contrast. Since it went to the מנחה instead, perhaps there is no such distinction.

keyTerms.meaning: Instead of teaching…
Let it make the distinction within the same case
In what case is this said?
A flour offering

phrases.english: Rather than teaching that if he made a meal offering פיגול
it is susceptible to the impurity of food,
let it distinguish within the same case:
In what case is this said?
Where he made it פיגול during the slaughtering,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל פַּיגֵּל בִּזְרִיקָה – מְטַמֵּא טוּמְאַת אֳכָלִין!
phrases.english: but if he made it פיגול during the sprinkling, it is susceptible to the impurity of food!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּתָנֵי פִּיגֵּל בְּמִנְחָה מְטַמֵּא טוּמְאַת אֳכָלִין, לִיפְלוֹג בְּדִידַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the result reached in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that פיגול during זריקה is susceptible according to the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If such a distinction existed among animal sacrifices, the ברייתא would have taught it directly instead of switching to a מנחה.

steps.title: The מנחה case teaches a new point
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא needed the מנחה case to teach that even though קמיצה is like שחיטה, a פיגול מנחה is still susceptible, because the flour was fit to eat at the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא needed the case of a מנחה made פיגול to teach this: even though he made it פיגול at the קמיצה, and the קומץ of a מנחה is like the שחיטה of an animal, even so it is susceptible to the impurity of food, since it had a time when it was fit at the very beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the מנחה case was not just a contrast. It teaches its own new point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a מנחה made פיגול at the קמיצה is like an animal made פיגול at the שחיטה, so it should not be susceptible. The ברייתא teaches that it is still susceptible, because before it was made holy the flour was ordinary food that was fit to eat. That earlier moment counts as its שעת הכושר.

keyTerms.meaning: He needed it (to teach a new point)
Taking a handful from a מנחה, the main service of a flour offering
The handful taken from a מנחה
A moment when something was fit to eat
Since

steps.whatToRemember: An animal made פיגול at שחיטה never had a fit moment, so it is not susceptible to טומאת אוכלין. A מנחה is susceptible even if made פיגול at the קמיצה, because the flour was fit to eat before it became holy.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that being susceptible to טומאת אוכלין depends on whether the item ever had a שעת הכושר, not only on when the פיגול thought happened.

phrases.english: The case of a meal offering made פיגול was needed by him,
to teach that even though he made it פיגול at the removal of the handful,
and the handful of a meal offering is like slaughtering,
even so, it is susceptible to the impurity of food,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְהָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר מֵעִיקָּרוֹ.
phrases.english: since it had a time of fitness from its beginning.
phrases.notes: Before it was made holy, it was just regular flour that anyone could eat.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the case teaches a needed new point (איצטריך)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מנחה case seemed to be only a contrast, so the ברייתא should have used the closer contrast of פיגול during זריקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מנחה case teaches that even פיגול at קמיצה, which is like שחיטה, is susceptible because the flour had an earlier שעת הכושר.

steps.title: רב אשי: we say 'he could redeem,' but not 'he could sprinkle'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer. Even when the meat was truly left overnight, or the פיגול thought came during the זריקה, רבי שמעון would not count the blood as already sprinkled. His idea only works for redeeming, not for sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I said this teaching before רב נחמן. Even if you say it was really left overnight, and even if you say he made it פיגול during the sprinkling, it still works. We say 'if he wanted, he could redeem it.' We do not say 'if he wanted, he would have sprinkled it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a new way to answer the whole problem from the earlier steps. He does not need to say the case was פיגול during שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps assumed that for רבי שמעון, blood that is ready to be sprinkled counts as sprinkled. רב אשי rejects that assumption. Redeeming is easy, so we treat it as already done. Sprinkling is not treated that way. So the meat never had a time when it was fit to eat, and the ברייתא works even in the hardest cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or discussion
Truly left overnight, not just in a loose sense
Redeems
If he wanted to

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two 'if he wanted' ideas. רב אשי says רבי שמעון uses it only for redeeming (פדיון). He never uses it for sprinkling blood (זריקה).
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the whole picture of רבי שמעון's rule. It removes the need for the answers given in steps 2 through 5.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I said this teaching in front of Rav Nachman:
Even if you say it was really left overnight,
and even if you say he made it פיגול during the sprinkling,
phrases.notes: He means: even in these cases, the offering still never had a time when it was fit to eat.

phrases.english: because 'if he wanted, he could redeem it' — that we say;

phrases.aramaic: אִי בָּעֵי הֲוָה זָרֵיק – לָא אָמְרִינַן.
phrases.english: 'if he wanted, he would have sprinkled it' — that we do not say.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַמְרִיתַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the קשיא of step 1, replacing the approach of steps 2–5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows רבי שמעון's rule: it covers redeeming only, not sprinkling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבי שמעון, blood that is ready to be sprinkled counts as already sprinkled.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון only treats redeeming as already done. Sprinkling is not treated as done, so the meat never had a fit time.

steps.title: A challenge from רבי יהושע's rule about מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי with רבי יהושע's rule. If an offering had a time when the כהנים were allowed to eat it, there is no מעילה. If it never had such a time, there is מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection. רבי יהושע stated a rule: any offering that had a time when it was permitted to the כהנים, one does not commit מעילה with it. Any offering that never had a time when it was permitted to the כהנים, one does commit מעילה with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to challenge רב אשי. This step is setting up the challenge; its full force comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on one question: was there ever a time when the כהנים could eat the offering (שעת היתר)? If yes, the offering left the category of fully holy property, so there is no מעילה. The גמרא will use this rule to test רב אשי's claim about what counts as a 'fit time'.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule
A time when it was permitted, meaning fit to be eaten
One is guilty of מעילה (using holy property for personal benefit)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
phrases.notes: This comes from the משנה at the very start of מסכת מעילה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua stated a rule:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁהָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר לַכֹּהֲנִים –
phrases.english: any offering that had a time when it was permitted to the כהנים,
one does not commit מעילה with it;

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר לַכֹּהֲנִים –
phrases.english: and any offering that never had a time when it was permitted to the כהנים,
one does commit מעילה with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge against רב אשי's answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim about when an offering counts as having had a fit time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע's rule turns on whether the offering ever had a שעת היתר. The examples that follow will test whether this fits רב אשי.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's examples of a permitted time: left overnight, impure, or taken out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע explains what counts as an offering that had a time permitted to the כהנים. His examples are one that was left overnight, one that became impure, and one that went out of the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is an offering that had a time when it was permitted to the כהנים? One that was left overnight, one that became impure, and one that went out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the cases it means by 'had a permitted time.' This is still part of the setup for the גמרא's challenge to רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these offerings became unfit only later, after it had already been fit for the כהנים. The key example for our discussion is 'שלנה', left overnight. That is the very case רב אשי was talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: One that was left overnight (נותר)
One that became ritually impure
One that went out of its allowed area, the courtyard

phrases.english: And what counts as a time permitted to the כהנים?
One that was left overnight, one that became impure, and one that went out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the source that started the challenge in step 7, by listing its cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that a 'left overnight' offering may never have had a fit time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source lists 'שלנה' as a case that had a permitted time. The גמרא is preparing to show how this clashes with רב אשי.

steps.title: Offerings that never had a time permitted to the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע lists the offerings that never had a time when the כהנים could eat them. These are a פיגול-type thought about time or place during slaughter, or blood received and sprinkled by disqualified people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which offering never had a time permitted to the כהנים? One slaughtered with a thought to eat it after its time or outside its place, or one whose blood was received and sprinkled by people not fit to serve.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי יהושע's rule, which it is using to challenge רב אשי. This is the second half of the quote, and it sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In these cases the offering was ruined from the very start, so the meat was never allowed to the כהנים. That is why there is מעילה here. These cases stand opposite the first list (left overnight, impure, went out), where there is no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Beyond its time. A thought during the service to eat it after the allowed time.
Outside its place. A thought to eat it outside the allowed area.
People who are not fit to do the Temple service.

phrases.english: And which is one that did not have
a time permitted to the priests?
One that was slaughtered with intent beyond its time,
or outside its place,
or where disqualified people received
and sprinkled its blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר לַכֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יהושע's two-part list. Step 8 gave the 'had a time' cases, and this step gives the 'never had a time' cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is part of the source being set up against רב אשי. The actual attack comes in the next step.

steps.title: Left overnight before sprinkling still has no מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads 'left overnight' as a case where the blood was never sprinkled. Since there is still no מעילה, 'he could have sprinkled' seems to count as sprinkling, which goes against רב אשי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first part lists 'left overnight, became impure, went out.' Doesn't this mean truly left overnight, blood and all? Then this is a case of 'if he wanted he could have sprinkled,' and still there is no מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: Here the גמרא makes the actual challenge against רב אשי, using the first half of רבי יהושע's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said the idea of 'if he wanted he could have' does not work for sprinkling. Suppose the offering was left overnight before the blood was sprinkled. The only reason it 'had a time permitted' would be that he could have sprinkled it in time. So רבי יהושע treats potential sprinkling as real sprinkling, which is the opposite of רב אשי.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a teaching.
Truly left overnight, meaning the blood too, before any sprinkling.
If he had wanted, he could have sprinkled.
There is no liability for מעילה (misusing holy property).

phrases.english: In any event, the first part teaches
one left overnight, one that became impure, and one that went out.
Is it not that it was truly left overnight,
phrases.notes: Truly left overnight means the blood too, so it was never sprinkled at all.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא דְּאִי בָּעֵי הֲוָה זָרֵיק הוּא,
phrases.english: and here it is a case of 'if he wanted, he could have sprinkled,'
and it teaches that there is no מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the source quoted in steps 7-9 to attack רב אשי's answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that 'if he wanted he could have' does not apply to sprinkling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no מעילה even when the offering was left overnight before sprinkling. That only makes sense if potential sprinkling counts as real sprinkling.

steps.title: The cases happened after the blood was sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהושע's cases happened after the sprinkling, when the meat was already fit to eat. So they were really permitted, not just potentially.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means it went out when it was already fit to go out, became impure when it was already fit to become impure, and was left overnight when it was already fit to be left over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אשי by reading רבי יהושע's cases differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Fit' here means the blood was already sprinkled, so the meat was truly allowed to the כהנים. The problem happened only after that. In these cases nobody needs the 'he could have sprinkled' idea, so רב אשי stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit, already in a state where this could properly happen.
To become impure.
To be left overnight.

phrases.english: No, it was fit to go out,
phrases.notes: Fit means the blood was already sprinkled, so the meat was already allowed when the problem happened.

phrases.english: and fit to become impure,
and fit to be left overnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by redefining the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the problems happened after the sprinkling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Left overnight' means before sprinkling, so potential sprinkling counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Left overnight' means after sprinkling, when the meat was truly permitted, so רב אשי is not contradicted.

steps.title: Then what about a real overnight case, and why such general wording?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. If a real overnight case before sprinkling would have מעילה, why does רבי יהושע use the broad wording 'had a time permitted' and 'did not have a time permitted'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But a true overnight case, what is the law? Would there really be מעילה? Then what about this wording, 'any that had a time permitted to the כהנים' and 'any that did not have a time permitted to the כהנים'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given in step 11. It questions how it fits רבי יהושע's exact wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following the answer, an offering truly left overnight before sprinkling would have מעילה. But רבי יהושע speaks in sweeping terms about whether it 'had a time' of being permitted. His 'never had a time' list includes only cases that were ruined from the start. This suggests that an offering which could have been sprinkled counts as having had such a time, and that goes back against רב אשי.

keyTerms.meaning: So indeed? A way of asking whether we really accept this result.
There is liability for מעילה.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of 'left overnight.' Step 11 means left overnight after sprinkling. This step asks about left overnight before sprinkling.

phrases.english: But a real leaving overnight, what is the law?
So indeed there is מעילה!
Then what of this: 'any that had
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is the regular printed wording. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: a time permitted to the priests'
and 'any that did not have
a time permitted to the priests'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל לִינָה מַמָּשׁ, מַאי? הָכִי נָמֵי דְּמוֹעֲלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 11 by asking how it fits רבי יהושע's general wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 11, and through it רב אשי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a real overnight case has מעילה, the broad 'had a time / never had a time' wording does not fit well. The wording points to potential permission being what matters.

steps.title: The wording the משנה should have used
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its challenge. If only offerings that were really permitted escape מעילה, the משנה should have said 'any offering that has a time permitted.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה should have said: 'Any offering that has a time permitted to the כהנים has no מעילה, and any offering that does not have a time permitted to the כהנים has מעילה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question from the last step by spelling out the wording the משנה should have used if the answer in step 11 were right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested wording speaks about real, present permission. Since the משנה instead says 'had a time permitted,' it seems to mean that even an offering that only could have become permitted (the blood could have been sprinkled) has no מעילה. That supports the challenge against רב אשי.

keyTerms.meaning: A time when the meat was permitted to be eaten
One is liable for מעילה, misusing holy property
He should have said

phrases.english: "Any offering that has a time permitted to the priests,
phrases.notes: Notice 'has' here, while the משנה said 'had.' The גמרא is pointing to that difference.

phrases.english: one is not liable for misusing it,"

phrases.aramaic: וְ״כֹל שֶׁאֵין לָהּ שְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר לַכֹּהֲנִים
phrases.english: and "any offering that does not have a time permitted to the priests,
one is liable for misusing it": that is what he should have said!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 12 by giving the alternative wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 11, that רבי יהושע only meant offerings already sprinkled and really permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only real permission counted, the משנה would have said 'has a time permitted.' Its broader wording shows that potential permission is enough to remove מעילה.

steps.title: רב אשי: you cannot compare מעילה to impurity
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a new answer. He accepts the point about מעילה but says it proves nothing about טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: Are you raising a contradiction from the laws of מעילה against the laws of טומאה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי opens a new defense. He is setting up the explanation that comes in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows the earlier answer is dropped. רב אשי now agrees that for מעילה, 'he could have sprinkled' counts. But he argues that the rules of מעילה and the rules of food impurity are built on different ideas, so one cannot prove the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Misusing holy property, which brings a penalty
Ritual impurity
You are raising a contradiction (comparing two things that seem to clash)

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Are you raising a contradiction between misuse and impurity?

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא אמר רב אשי מעילה אטומאה קא רמית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed answer of step 11 with a new answer that separates the two areas of law.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between two areas of law (מעילה versus טומאה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since 'he could have sprinkled' removes מעילה, it should also give the meat the status of food for טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two laws depend on different things, so a rule about מעילה does not decide טומאה.

steps.title: מעילה depends on holiness, which cannot return
steps.stepSummary: מעילה is about whether the item is still fully holy. Once that holiness has left, nothing brings it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: מעילה depends on whether something is holy or not holy. After its holiness has left, how could it come back and rest on it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains the מעילה side: once the blood was fit to be sprinkled, the holiness that causes מעילה is gone for good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As soon as the blood could be sprinkled, the offering counts as permitted to the כהנים, and its מעילה-holiness leaves. If the offering later becomes disqualified, for example by being left overnight, that holiness does not come back. That is why the משנה says 'had a time permitted.'

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness that makes an item belong fully to Heaven
Lapsed, went away
Comes back and rests on it again

phrases.aramaic: מְעִילָה מִשּׁוּם קְדוּשָּׁה וְלָאו קְדוּשָּׁה הִיא,
phrases.english: Misuse depends on whether it is holy or not holy;
after its holiness has lapsed,
by what means could it come back and rest on it?
phrases.notes: Literally 'ride on it.' He means the holiness has nothing to bring it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: מעילה משום קדושה ולאו קדושה היא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of רב אשי's distinction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A later disqualification might bring back the holiness and the מעילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once holiness lapses, which happens when the blood could be sprinkled, it is gone permanently.

steps.title: Food impurity depends on whether it is food right now
steps.stepSummary: טומאת אוכלין depends on whether the meat counts as food. That depends on whether the blood can be sprinkled, not on whether it once could have been.
steps.simpleTranslation: Impurity depends on whether something is food or not food. Wherever he is able to sprinkle the blood if he wants, that makes the meat food, and it can become impure with food impurity. Where he wants to sprinkle but cannot, it is not made food, and it does not become impure with food impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains the טומאה side and finishes his answer. Food status is not locked in the way the loss of holiness is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food status follows the present situation. While the blood can still be sprinkled, the meat counts as food. Once the offering is disqualified so the blood can no longer be sprinkled, it is not food, even though it could have been sprinkled earlier. So the משנה about מעילה does not contradict רב אשי's view on טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Food
The impurity that applies to food
Makes it into, gives it the status of
Sprinkles (the blood on the altar)

steps.whatToRemember: מעילה goes away for good once the blood could be sprinkled, because lost holiness never comes back. Food status for טומאה depends on whether the blood can still be sprinkled, so a later disqualification takes it away.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב אשי rejects the משנה about מעילה. He accepts that 'he could have sprinkled' removes מעילה. He only denies that this decides food impurity.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that one fact, like whether the blood could be sprinkled, can work differently in different areas of law. It depends on what each law is really about.

phrases.aramaic: טוּמְאָה מִשּׁוּם אוּכְלָא וְלָאו (מִשּׁוּם) אוּכְלָא הִיא,
phrases.english: Impurity depends on whether it is food or not food;
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the regular printed wording, but the corrected wording leaves it out.

phrases.english: anywhere that if he wants to sprinkle
he is able to sprinkle it,
that gives it the status of food,
and it can become impure with the impurity of food.
Where if he wants to sprinkle
he cannot sprinkle,
it does not give it the status of food,
and it does not become impure with the impurity of food.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording. Some versions don't have it.

steps.triggerLanguage: טומאה משום אוכלא ולאו משום אוכלא היא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second half of רב אשי's distinction and completes his answer to the challenge from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the basis of טומאת אוכלין, which is different from מעילה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the blood could have been sprinkled, the meat should count as food forever, just as מעילה goes away forever.
steps.terutzMaskana: Food status depends on whether the blood can be sprinkled. If it can no longer be sprinkled, the meat is not food and does not receive food impurity.

steps.title: Opening a challenge from the case of an uncertain guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if someone brings an אשם תלוי and then learns he never sinned, and he learns this before it is slaughtered, רבי מאיר says the animal goes back to the flock as an ordinary animal. Then it starts to quote חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: Someone brings an אשם תלוי and then finds out he did not sin. If he found out before it was slaughtered, the animal goes out and grazes with the flock. This is רבי מאיר's view. And חכמים say:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new challenge against רב אשי by quoting a משנה. This step only sets up the case. The part of the משנה that makes the challenge comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם תלוי is brought only because the person is unsure whether he sinned. Once he learns he did not sin, the offering has no reason to exist. רבי מאיר says that if he found out before the slaughter, the animal simply becomes ordinary again. The גמרא is laying out the case step by step so it can later use another stage of this משנה against רב אשי's rule about blood that is ready to be sprinkled.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'provisional' guilt offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he did a sin that needs a חטאת
It became known that he did not sin
Before it was slaughtered
It goes out and grazes with the flock, meaning it becomes an ordinary, non-holy animal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not expect the challenge to be clear yet. This step only quotes the beginning of the משנה; the line that actually challenges רב אשי comes in the next part.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: One who brings a provisional guilt offering,
phrases.notes: This offering is brought when a person isn't sure whether he sinned. See ויקרא 5:17–19.

phrases.english: and it became known that he did not sin –

phrases.aramaic: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁחַט נוֹדַע לוֹ,
phrases.english: if it became known to him before it was slaughtered,
it goes out and grazes in the flock,
phrases.notes: In other words, the animal goes back to being ordinary, because it was made holy by mistake.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Rabbis say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב אשי's answer (steps 14–16), the גמרא brings a new source to challenge his position.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's view that for טומאת אוכלין, blood that is ready to be sprinkled is not treated as if it were sprinkled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The גמרא sets up a משנה about an אשם תלוי that turns out to be unnecessary. A later stage of this case will be used to show how the meat is treated based on the blood's status, which seems to clash with רב אשי.
